catch_age_evidence: The 2024 update fits the BAM statistical catch-age model through 2023. It updates commercial handline, headboat, and general recreational landings and discards. survey_age_evidence: The fitted assessment uses five aggregate abundance indices: commercial handline, headboat, headboat discards, SERFS chevron trap, and SERFS video. weights_evidence: The SEDAR 73 life-history table provides input growth curves and length-to-whole-weight relationships used to derive weight at age. The 2024 update retains the SEDAR 73 model configuration.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is a fixed input logistic curve with a supplied age-specific vector. The SEDAR 73 model calculates spawning output as eggs using maturity, female proportion, batches at age, and size-based fecundity; this is not conventional SSB in biomass units.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed over time and decreases with age using a Lorenzen curve. It is scaled to match cumulative survival over ages 4 through the oldest observed age (51) under constant M = 0.11 per year.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. A fractional within-year timing for the fitted survey indices is not specified in the reviewed production report.
output_evidence: The 2024 report publishes annual numbers at age (1000 fish), biomass at age (1000 lb), and instantaneous F at age (per year) for 1950-2023; the model age range is 1-20+, with age 20 as the plus group. catch_age_evidence: The latest full accepted age-structured run located is SEDAR 67 (Stock SMART run 10102), an operational Stock Synthesis model with data through 2017. Its Appendix A prints the final SS3 input files. Commercial east and west handline catch is in metric tons; recreational catch is in thousands of fish. The model fits commercial east and west and aggregated Gulf-wide recreational age compositions, with modeled ages 0-14 (age 14 is a plus group; fishery recruitment and fishing begin at age 1). Age-specific catch can be reconstructed from catch totals and these compositions.
survey_age_evidence: The 2020 model uses aggregate fishery-dependent and fishery-independent indices, including headboat CPUE, SEAMAP larval, combined video, and SEAMAP summer groundfish series. Survey likelihoods are not age-specific abundance indices; survey compositions are length-based. The 2023 Gulf interim analysis uses an updated G-FISHER video index to review catch advice and is not a replacement age-structured assessment.
weights_evidence: Growth and length-weight relationships are fixed from SEDAR 45 and retained in SEDAR 67. Age-specific weights can be derived from the run-specific growth and length-weight inputs; the model-ready values should be checked against the printed Appendix A and Table 2.
maturity_evidence: The report gives the fixed maturity relationship and spawning biology. The model defines spawning output as egg production, using female proportion, maturity, batch fecundity, and spawning frequency, rather than conventional biomass SSB.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is a fixed age-specific Lorenzen vector, scaled to average M = 0.25. Age-0 mortality is adjusted for the assumed midyear birth date.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual, single-season, and assumes fishing and spawning occur continuously through the year. Exact within-year timing for each survey index is not established by the reviewed report and should not be inferred from annual frequency.
output_evidence: Table 18 reports annual total biomass (metric tons), spawning output (eggs), total abundance (thousands of fish), and recruitment (thousands of fish) through 2017. Tables 16-17 report fleet fishing mortality and harvest rate, not F-at-age. N-at-age appears only as a figure; no numeric N-at-age or F-at-age series or population-output uncertainty table was located.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation as a distinct Gulf of Mexico unit. The latest Stock SMART row is a 2023 Stock Monitoring Update whose review outcome is “Accept previous approach, remand new attempt”; the 2023 Gulf SSC interim analysis used G-FISHER to consider catch advice and its motion to accept the analysis and recommend updated catch advice failed. Neither establishes a new accepted age-structured assessment. The latest full accepted age-structured run located is the 2020 SEDAR 67 Stock Synthesis assessment through 2017, with final model input files and numerical aggregate outputs in its report. It is eligible for detailed source curation, with age-specific survey indices and numeric N/F-at-age outputs absent from the reviewed public sources. A February 2025 committee summary records the Gulf Council recommendation for an update in 2027; this is a future recommendation, not a completed assessment.
notes: Do not combine the 2023 interim index update with the 2020 SEDAR 67 likelihood or outputs. The same species has a separate NOAA:10257 Southern Atlantic Coast management unit; the Gulf and South Atlantic entries remain separate. SEDAR 67 outputs are point estimates without population-series uncertainty in Table 18; the report provides no numeric N-at-age/F-at-age arrays. The August 2025 committee summary places its vermilion snapper assessment scheduled outside SEDAR under the South Atlantic section, so it was not used as evidence about this Gulf unit. No canonical database values were imported.

catch_age_evidence: The latest accepted full assessment located is SEDAR 55 (2018), a Beaufort statistical catch-at-age update through 2016. It fits annual landings from five fleets and age compositions for commercial handline, headboat, general recreational, and SERFS chevron trap samples. Landings are in 1,000 lb whole weight for commercial fleets and 1,000 fish for recreational fleets. Composition ages are calendar ages 1-12+ with age 12 as the plus group; sample years vary and years below the assessment sample threshold were excluded. Total landings and documented weighted age compositions support a source-based catch-at-age reconstruction, but the compositions are not themselves observed catch numbers-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment includes age compositions from the fishery-independent SERFS chevron-trap survey for 1990-2016, at ages 1-12+. It fits aggregate abundance indices, including the combined SERFS trap/video series and the MARMAP Florida snapper-trap series (1983-1987); the MARMAP index had no age compositions. The model therefore has age composition plus aggregate index information, not an age-specific abundance index.
weights_evidence: Growth parameters were estimated externally and treated as fixed inputs: von Bertalanffy L-infinity = 506 mm, K = 0.12/year, and t0 = -3.5 years. Whole weight at age is derived from total length in mm using WW = 2.1e-5 * TL^2.91; the report tabulates life-history characteristics at age.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is age-specific: 91% at age 1 and 99-100% at ages 2-12+. The assessment models spawning stock as egg production, including female proportion, batch fecundity, and age-specific spawning frequency; it is not conventional SSB biomass.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed and decreases with age following the Lorenzen relationship. The age-specific vector is scaled to match cumulative survival through age 19 under constant M = 0.22/year; an alternative Charnov form is a sensitivity only.
timing_evidence: The model is annual and computes spawning stock at the midpoint of the year. Index predictions use population numbers at midyear (or weight at age for commercial handline). Specific survey-month timing was not established by the reviewed assessment sources.
output_evidence: The report gives numerical base-run total abundance-at-age (Table 6; 1,000 fish; ages 1-12+), biomass-at-age (Table 7; 1,000 lb whole weight), and F-at-age (Table 11; per year) over the historical assessment, alongside annual recruitment, total biomass, egg-production spawning stock, and status indicators. The MCB analysis reports uncertainty for selected aggregate/status outputs; age-specific uncertainty was not located in the tables.
decision_reason: Eligible for detailed source curation as a distinct South Atlantic management unit. SEDAR 55 is the latest accepted full assessment found (assessment year 2018; data through 2016). The 2023 interim analysis was not accepted for catch advice because its index-based approach did not fit the index or inform the assessment population estimates. An updated assessment is planned outside SEDAR in 2027 and has not yet produced a completed run.
notes: NOAA:10257 is the South Atlantic unit and must remain separate from NOAA:10256, the Gulf of Mexico unit of the same species. The 2026 draft terms of reference and September 2026 assessment schedule identify a future update; they do not replace SEDAR 55 outputs. The age-composition and landings inputs are suitable for a documented catch-at-age reconstruction, with official fleet units and weighting preserved. Spawning stock is in eggs. No canonical data were imported and no tinyAM translation was attempted. The review files are cached in the gitignored source_cache directory with retrieval dates and SHA-256 checksums.

stock_name: Black sea bass - Southern Atlantic Coast
assessment_area: South Atlantic U.S. waters, Cape Hatteras to Florida
catch_age_evidence: The SEDAR 76 Update used five fleets with annual landings by weight, discard mortalities by number, and fleet age/length compositions. Age compositions are not available in every year; length compositions fill some gaps. The report does not provide the full numerical annual composition arrays, and a run-matched machine-readable data package was not verified.
survey_age_evidence: The update fitted two fishery-independent and two fishery-dependent abundance indices. It includes survey age compositions in some years, but the complete numerical age-composition inputs were not located.
weights_evidence: The model uses length-at-age and weight-at-age derived from a von Bertalanffy growth curve and length-weight relationship; life-history values are tabulated.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is age-based and male transition is age-based; the update uses age-specific mature weight for spawning biomass.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed over time and declines with age using a Lorenzen relationship rescaled to a constant fully selected M of 0.375 per year.
timing_evidence: The model uses annual time steps and annual fishery and survey series. A fractional within-year timing for the abundance indices was not verified.
output_evidence: The 2025 update tabulates estimated N-at-age and total F-at-age, as well as biomass, recruitment, and estimated landings-at-age. M is an assumed input, not an estimated age-specific output.
decision_reason: The latest public detailed assessment is the 2025 SEDAR 76 Update, based on data through 2023. It documents age-structured inputs and age-specific outputs, but the full run-matched numerical composition inputs were not verified. A revision was scheduled for late 2026 and SEDAR 108 is underway; keep eligibility unresolved until the current run and complete inputs are pinned.
notes: The Council/SSC used the 2025 update for ABC advice, while the September 2026 proposed rule describes a further revision in progress and a pending formal status determination. The 2025 report provides N-at-age, F-at-age, and SSB tables, but does not expose complete annual age-composition matrices in machine-readable form. catch_age_evidence: The accepted 2025 management-track assessment updates commercial and recreational catch data. The multi-WHAM framework uses aggregate removals and age-composition information, but the complete 2025 run-matched catch and age-composition matrices were not located in the public report and peer-review materials reviewed.
survey_age_evidence: The 2025 update includes state and federal survey indices and a VAST combined index. The assessment framework uses numbers-at-age states; complete survey age inputs and the run-specific age-length-key files were not verified.
weights_evidence: The 2025 assessment report summary identifies age-specific weights as model inputs, but the final run-matched numerical matrices were not recovered.
maturity_evidence: The 2025 assessment report summary identifies age-specific maturity as a model input, but the final run-matched numerical schedules were not recovered.
mortality_evidence: The management-track update retains age-structured population dynamics and age-specific natural mortality for projections; the complete run-specific mortality specification was not verified from the public summary materials.
timing_evidence: The model combines spatially and seasonally stratified survey information into regional indices; the fractional within-year timing used for each index was not verified.
output_evidence: The 2025 accepted assessment reports SSB, fully selected F, and recruitment through 2024. Peer review discusses random-effects numbers-at-age, but the complete numerical N-at-age and F-at-age output series were not located.
decision_reason: The 2025 management-track assessment was peer reviewed and accepted as best scientific information for the Mid-Atlantic stock, with data through 2024. Public summaries confirm an age-structured multi-WHAM model and age-specific biology, but do not provide sufficient run-matched numerical inputs or full age-specific outputs to verify translation readiness.
notes: The 2025 panel report states the assessment updates the 2024 multi-WHAM model through 2024 and was accepted. The detailed assessment report link cited by the draft points to NOAA SASINF; the final run package and its data files remain to be recovered. The model contains north/south subregions divided near Hudson Canyon; this is one Mid-Atlantic management stock, not two inventory units. See discovery/source_reviews/ noaa_black_sea_bass_mid_atlantic_2025.md.

catch_age_evidence: The independent review states that the 2016 assessment had no age structure in catch data. The assessment used an age composition from only 22 adult research-fishery fish, which is not an annual fishery catch-at-age series.
survey_age_evidence: The four abundance indices are aggregate: three recreational catch-per-trip series and one SCUBA visual index. No age-specific survey series is reported; the small research age sample is not an index-at-age.
weights_evidence: The SEDAR report tabulates modeled mid-year weight-at-age in kg for ages 0-40. This is a model-derived biological curve, not a complete annual observed weight-at-age input series.
maturity_evidence: The report describes strong assumptions in reproductive functions and says age/size at maturity and fecundity information are insufficient across the stock range; no complete observed maturity-at-age input series was located.
mortality_evidence: The 2016 models use constant natural mortality despite documented episodic cold-kill events; the review identifies this as a structural concern. No supported time-varying M series was located.
timing_evidence: The reviewed report presents aggregate annual indices but does not specify fractional-year survey timing. The current FWC monitoring framework uses alternative population indicators rather than a full-scale traditional age-structured assessment.
output_evidence: SEDAR 47 reports outputs from two age-structured production models, but the review panel concluded they were not adequate for status inferences or management advice; NOAA Stock SMART records both 2016 entries as rejected. These are not accepted comparable official outputs for this audit.
decision_reason: Ineligible for the age-disaggregated source set. The latest detailed 2016 SEDAR 47 benchmark was rejected as too uncertain for management use. Its catch data have no age structure, and the only reported adult age sample contains 22 research-fishery fish; aggregate indices do not supply age-specific abundance observations. FWC now uses alternative management goals and indicators rather than a full-scale traditional assessment.
notes: Stock SMART IDs 10315 and 11042 point to the same 2016 SEDAR 47 assessment family; the assessed population is Southeastern U.S., not two independent Gulf-only and coastwide model units. The older 2010 Stock SMART row for 11042 is separate and was only partially accepted for status determinations. This is a discovery screen only; no canonical data have been imported.

catch_age_evidence: The November 2023 operational assessment uses annual nominal age compositions for commercial vertical-line and longline fleets in eastern and western Gulf areas; sex samples were pooled because of data quality and sample-size limits. Age bins are 1-year bins with a 40+ group. WP-04 reports annual sample counts and plots age proportions, but the reviewed public documents do not provide the full numerical composition arrays or model input file.
survey_age_evidence: The NMFS Bottom Longline Survey provides aggregate eastern and western Gulf abundance indices for 2000-2021 with CVs and confidence limits, plus survey age compositions over the same years. WP-09 tabulates the aggregate index values; the numerical age composition vectors were not recovered. The indices are not age-specific abundance series.
weights_evidence: The report documents regional von Bertalanffy growth and a fixed gutted-weight to total-length relationship, so weight-at-age is derivable from the model biology. The exact run-matched biological parameter and surface files were not located.
maturity_evidence: The assessment retains the SEDAR 22 logistic maturity and protogynous transition assumptions; all male or transitioning fish are treated as mature. The model input file needed to verify the exact run-specific maturity values was not located.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality follows a Lorenzen size-dependent schedule, with the SEDAR 22 reference estimate M = 0.073 retained. Region-specific age schedules depend on growth; exact model input values were not recovered.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual and assumes fishing is continuous and homogeneous through the year. The bottom-longline survey is conducted in August in the eastern Gulf and September in the western Gulf, but exact within-year timing values from the fitted model input were not located.
output_evidence: The final report and 2024 executive summary provide annual SSB, recruitment, and exploitation outputs, including uncertainty summaries. Full numeric annual N-at-age and F-at-age output arrays were not verified in the reviewed public files.
decision_reason: The latest official fitted assessment located is SEDAR 85, completed in November 2023 with data through 2021. The 2024 SSC executive summary and additional projections use that fitted assessment rather than a new population-model run. The report confirms age compositions, aggregate survey indices, age-based biology, and comparable population outputs. Eligibility remains unresolved because exact age-composition vectors, model timing, and run-matched input/output arrays were not available in the reviewed public sources.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART row 10323 is the Gulf of Mexico management unit; SEDAR 85 treats the east and west Gulf subregions as model areas within one stock, not separate candidate stock units. The Stock SMART inventory year 2024 corresponds to the SSC review of the 2023 operational fit. Source PDFs are cached in the ignored source_cache/noaa_yellowedge_sedar85_2023/ directory with URL and checksum provenance.

catch_age_evidence: The 2022 Gulf operational assessment includes nominal annual age compositions for commercial vertical-line and longline, recreational charter/private, and headboat fleets. Table 4 provides annual fish/trip sample counts; exact model age bins and observed vectors still need native-file or other source recovery.

weights_evidence: The report specifies a fixed gutted-weight-to-fork-length relationship and a size-modified von Bertalanffy growth curve. These support derivation of weight-at-age, but the exact run-matched age-weight surface has not been recovered.

mortality_evidence: The report specifies an age-specific Lorenzen-scaled natural-mortality vector; the numerical run-matched vector remains to be extracted.

decision_reason: The 2022 SEDAR 68OA is the latest full production assessment located. The 2025 projection report updates advice projections from the earlier fitted assessment, rather than providing a new population-model fit. Source PDFs are in the ignored source_cache/noaa_scamp_sedar68oa/ with URL and checksum provenance.

assessment_area: U.S. Caribbean: Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands
catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 35 (2014) uses fishery landings, effort, and annual length-frequency data. The report does not provide catch-at-age observations; age is used only to construct life-history and per-recruit calculations.
survey_age_evidence: SEDAR 35 reports standardized fishery CPUE and a SEAMAP-C relative-abundance index from southwest Puerto Rico, plus spawning-aggregation density series. These indices are aggregate and not age-specific abundance observations.
weights_evidence: Published length-weight relationships support per-recruit sensitivity analyses. The report does not document a model-ready annual weight-at-age input for an age-structured population model.
maturity_evidence: The SEDAR 35 spawner-per-recruit analysis assumes knife-edge maturity at age 3. This is a reference-point calculation, not an age-specific maturity surface used in a population time-series model.
mortality_evidence: Current total mortality is estimated from length data using a mean-length mortality estimator; fishing mortality is derived as Z minus natural mortality. Natural mortality is based on a maximum-age method. SEDAR 46 later applies length-based methods to six different Caribbean species-island units, not red hind.
timing_evidence: The assessment reports annual fishery CPUE and aggregate SEAMAP-C abundance observations. It does not specify timing for an age-specific survey index.
output_evidence: SEDAR 35 reports CPUE indices, length-based mortality estimates, and per-recruit reference-point calculations. It does not provide annual abundance-at-age, fishing mortality-at-age, natural mortality-at-age, recruitment, or spawning-biomass series for comparison.
decision_reason: SEDAR 35 (2014) is the latest completed red-hind-specific assessment located. SEDAR 46 (2016) reviewed 36 candidate species-island units but assessed six different units; red hind was not among them. The newer SEDAR 91 reports disseminated in 2025 concern US Caribbean spiny lobster, not red hind. SEDAR 35 is length-based and neither it nor the later projects located supplies the age-disaggregated inputs and annual population outputs required for this comparison.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10327 represents Caribbean red hind. SEDAR 35 contains Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands information, and SEDAR 46 considered Caribbean island units separately; these subareas are not separate Stock SMART entries for this candidate. This discovery screen creates no canonical stock, assessment, input, or output records.

catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 88 uses commercial and recreational landings, discards, and weighted landings age compositions. Commercial handline ages cover 1991-2022, longline 1993-2022, trap 1991-2006 (pooled as a super-period), and recreational 1991-2022. Composition bins are annual ages with 20+ as the plus group; the composition figures and working papers require digitization for annual proportions.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment fits aggregate abundance indices and length compositions for the Combined Video Survey (1993-2022), SEAMAP Summer Groundfish Survey (2009-2022), and NMFS Bottom Longline Survey (2001-2022). It does not list age compositions or age-specific indices for these surveys. Do not derive survey-age observations from fitted selectivity or population states.
weights_evidence: The model uses a fixed weight-length relationship and an estimated age-growth curve; it does not report an independently observed annual stock-weight-at-age input series. A weight-at-age surface would be derived from model biology, not a direct source observation.
maturity_evidence: Maturity and female-to-male transition schedules are carried forward from the SEDAR 42 benchmark; the model fixes fecundity-at-age as relative egg production. This differs from a conventional mature-biomass SSB definition.
mortality_evidence: M is a time-invariant, age-dependent Lorenzen schedule. The point estimate is Mtarget = 5.4/29 = 0.186 using maximum age 29, with length-at-age determining the age pattern. Sensitivities use maximum ages 24 and 34.
timing_evidence: Seasonal timing is documented. The NMFS BLL uses August samples in the eastern GOM and September in the central and western GOM, with early October 2022 stations retained; the fitted SEAMAP index uses summer data. The video index pools surveys with differing sampling months. These windows do not define one fractional timing for each pooled model index.
output_evidence: Table 15 reports annual recruitment, total and exploitable biomass, exploitable abundance and SSB from 1986-2022. SSB is relative egg production, not biomass. Tables 13-14 report exploitation rates. Age-specific N and F are shown in figures, but numerical full surfaces and annual output uncertainty were not located.
decision_reason: SEDAR 88 is the latest full, accepted production assessment (completed in 2025, data through 2022). It provides age-composition inputs, aggregate abundance indices, biology and annual population outputs. The 2026 StockSMART monitoring row is marked Remand and is not a replacement production run. tinyAM eligibility remains unresolved because no fitted survey-age observations or single fractional timing for the pooled indices were found, and SSB is reported as egg production rather than biomass.
notes: The December 10, 2025 report revision corrects Tables 5, 7, 8 and 19; use this revision rather than the February 2025 release. StockSMART assessment 13943 records full acceptance for SEDAR 88; assessment 14350 is a 2026 stock monitoring update with review result Remand and the same terminal data year. NOAA Stock SMART 10332 is the distinct South Atlantic red grouper unit. See discovery/source_reviews/noaa_red_grouper_gom_2025.md.

assessment_area: U.S. South Atlantic red grouper management unit under the South Atlantic Fishery Management Council; North Carolina through the Atlantic side of the Florida Keys.
catch_age_evidence: The latest completed assessment used for South Atlantic stock status is SEDAR 53 (2017; data through 2015), a statistical catch-age BAM. It fits annual fleet landings/discards and age compositions for commercial lines, headboat, general recreational, and SERFS. SEDAR53-WP05 Table 3 publishes weighted commercial handline/longline age proportions for 1996-2015, ages 1-16 with 16+ pooled. Catch-at-age is not a complete direct input series; age-specific removals can be reconstructed only for fleet-years with matching catch totals and compositions. Preserve unsampled fleet-years as missing.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment fits an aggregate annual SERFS chevron-trap/video abundance index and SERFS age compositions. These support age-specific index reconstruction only over years with matching survey age compositions. Commercial handline and headboat abundance indices are aggregate, not age-indexed.
weights_evidence: Growth and weight-at-age are inputs summarized in SEDAR 53 Table 1. Total length follows a von Bertalanffy curve and whole weight is calculated as 8.418e-9 * TL^3.1; model ages are 1-16+.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is a fixed logistic ogive from SEDAR 19 inputs (50% maturity at age 2.8; age-1 females immature); all males are considered mature. Sex ratio is a fixed logistic ogive. SSB is total mature biomass of both sexes at peak spawning.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed over time and age-varying by the Lorenzen relationship, rescaled so cumulative survival through age 26 matches constant M=0.14. It is an assumed input, not an estimated M process.
timing_evidence: The model fits annual aggregate indices and seasonal fishery/survey source data. The report does not specify a single within-year fraction for all indices; source-specific seasonal timing must be retained or explicitly approximated during translation.
output_evidence: SEDAR 53 Table 6 reports start-of-year abundance at ages 1-16+ (1000 fish), including 1976-2015 and a 2016 forecast. Table 8 reports annual apical F (yr^-1), total biomass and peak-spawning SSB (mt) through 2015. The assessment also reports recruitment and uncertainty analyses; age-specific uncertainty is not tabulated in the reviewed source.
decision_reason: NOAA’s current stock page identifies the 2017 assessment as the South Atlantic stock assessment used for status; the planned SEDAR 86 operational update was not completed. SEDAR 53 provides a catch-age model, observed age compositions, biological/mortality assumptions, and comparable age-specific abundance and aggregate SSB/F outputs. Source quantities support age-specific reconstruction for overlapping fleet-years, with explicit gaps for fleets or years without age compositions. Timing and age-specific uncertainty remain translation/extraction limitations.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10332 is the South Atlantic management unit and is distinct from Gulf of Mexico red grouper (10331). The latest completed detailed assessment is SEDAR 53 (2017; terminal data year 2015); SEDAR 86 was not completed. The SEDAR 53 final report and commercial/recreational age-composition papers are cached with provenance and SHA-256 checksums under source_cache/discovery_noaa_red_grouper_sa_2017. This is a discovery eligibility screen only: no canonical assessment, input or output data were added.

catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 36 Update fits annual removals through 2018 for commercial handline, commercial longline, and a combined recreational fleet. Commercial input removals are in whole weight and recreational removals in numbers; landings and dead discards are combined. Annual fleet age-composition figures and sample sizes are reported; age 14 is the composition plus group. Exact fishery composition arrays were not recovered; catch-at-age requires documented digitization and reconstruction from removals and compositions.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment fits aggregate headboat, MARMAP chevron-trap, and vertical longline indices with annual CVs; the two fishery-independent indices cover 1996-2018. Age compositions for chevron trap and vertical longline are also used, with annual sample sizes. The report shows observed compositions in figures but does not provide numeric input matrices; an age-specific index would be a documented reconstruction, not a directly fitted index.
weights_evidence: Table 1 gives age-specific whole weight for model ages 1-25+, with age 25+ as the plus group. External growth and length-weight parameters were treated as inputs. The report distinguishes population weights from fishery quantities and documents the discard conversion.
maturity_evidence: Table 1 gives female maturity-at-age and proportion female for ages 1-25. Female maturity is zero at ages 1-2 and logistic from age 3+, with 50% maturity at 5.6 years; all males are treated as mature. Spawning biomass is total mature biomass, evaluated at mid-year peak spawning.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed in the base run and age-dependent under the Charnov relationship, scaled to M = 0.08 at maximum age 56. The MCB uncertainty analysis draws a scalar M from 0.05-0.12 and rescales the curve.
timing_evidence: The assessment uses annual time steps and assumes peak spawning at mid-year. Survey series are annual; a more precise within-year survey fraction is not reported in the assessment sources reviewed.
output_evidence: The revised report includes numeric annual abundance-at-age (Table 6), biomass-at-age (Table 7), status and SSB (Table 8), total F-at-age (Table 11), and estimated removals-at-age (Tables 12-15) through 2018. Outputs are base-run point estimates; annual age-specific uncertainty was not located.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation. SEDAR 36 Update is the latest completed assessment located for the current South Atlantic unit, published in 2021 with terminal year 2018; the draft 2027 statement of work still identifies it as the prior assessment. The report supplies annual removals, aggregate indices, age compositions, age-specific biology, and numeric abundance, biomass, recruitment, and fishing-mortality outputs. Fishery age-composition inputs require figure digitization, so reconstructed catch-at-age must be identified as approximate.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART row 10339 identifies the South Atlantic unit. The report uses both the current name Epinephelus niveatus and synonym Hyporthodus niveatus; neither is present as a canonical stock. Do not conflate with North Atlantic or Gulf units. SEDAR 36 WP15 contains code/data for the superseded 2013 assessment only and was not used as a substitute for update inputs. Update report and two 2020 update working papers are cached locally with URL, revision, retrieval time, byte-size, and SHA-256 provenance.

catch_age_evidence: The September 2022 SRFS run provides annual catch and discard totals by fleet, with inputs in numbers and biomass, and uses commercial and recreational age composition data through 2019. The SEDAR72-WP-17 report gives annual age-sample counts and composition figures; digitizing those figures is a documented source-based reconstruction, not an exact machine-readable input recovery.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment includes standardized fishery CPUE indices and age-0 and video survey abundance indices with annual uncertainty. The accepted run is an age-structured Stock Synthesis model with data bins age 0 through 20+; no full age-specific survey-index matrix was recovered.
weights_evidence: The October 2021 report provides the fixed sex-combined length-weight relationship and fitted growth curve; age-specific weights can be derived from those documented inputs. The 2022 SRFS run retains the assessment structure.
maturity_evidence: The October 2021 report documents fixed logistic female maturity (age at 50% maturity about 3.9 years; slope 2.513) and treats males and transitioning fish as mature. These assumptions are retained for the 2022 SRFS run.
mortality_evidence: The report supplies a fixed age-specific Lorenzen natural-mortality vector scaled to the Then et al. (2015) estimate M = 0.159 per year.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual and assumes fishing and data collection are continuous and homogeneous through the year, so it does not model seasonal removals. A single within-year survey fraction is not reported and would be an explicit translation approximation if needed.
output_evidence: The September 2022 report gives annual SSB, total and exploitable biomass, exploitable abundance, recruitment, fleet exploitation, parameters, and model fits for 1963-2019. The report does not provide complete annual N-at-age or F-at-age arrays in the recovered tables.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation. The latest accepted production run located is the SEDAR 72 amendment using Florida SRFS private-mode landings, completed in September 2022 with assessment data through 2019 and reviewed by the Gulf SSC. SEDAR 105 is underway in 2026, while NOAA continues to identify SEDAR 72 as the most recent population assessment. Catch totals, age-composition figures and sample counts, index series, fixed mortality and maturity assumptions, growth and weight information, and comparable annual outputs are available. Exact numeric age-composition arrays and run-matched native files were not recovered; the composition figures can support an explicitly documented digitization.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART row 10348 is Gulf Gag Grouper (Mycteroperca microlepis). Do not merge it with the distinct South Atlantic Gag unit (row 10349). The October 2021 base report was superseded for management use by the September 2022 SRFS run, which replaced Florida private-mode MRIP-FES catch inputs with calibrated SRFS estimates and corrected headboat data. Cache files are kept in the ignored source_cache/noaa_gag_sedar72_2022/ directory with URL and checksum provenance.

catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 71 reports annual removals by fleet for 1962-2019 and fleet age compositions through 2019, with observed and fitted age proportions shown in assessment figures and Tables 4-5 giving fish and trip sample sizes. Catch-at-age can be reconstructed from source totals and digitized observed compositions, but exact fishery composition arrays or run-matched native input files were not recovered.
survey_age_evidence: The fit uses aggregate headboat and SERFS video indices with annual CVs; the report tabulates them through 2019. SEDAR71-WP04 provides numeric chevron-trap age counts and proportions for 1990-2019. These age data inform the fitted selectivity of the video index; the report does not fit a direct age-specific survey index. Any age-index reconstruction is approximate.
weights_evidence: The assessment report provides age-specific whole weights and separate population and fishery growth curves; fleet catch-age numbers require the documented conversion from reported landings and age compositions.
maturity_evidence: The report provides female maturity-at-age and age-specific sex ratio; all males were treated as mature. Female age at 50% maturity was estimated at about 4.6 years.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed over time and declines with age using the Lorenzen relationship. The age curve is scaled over fully selected ages 5+ to match survival to age 30 under constant M = 0.15; an age-specific vector is reported.
timing_evidence: The population model uses annual time steps, with spawning biomass measured at peak spawning in mid-April. Chevron-trap sampling occurred May-September; a single within-year survey fraction is not specified in the assessment.
output_evidence: The report gives numeric annual total abundance-at-age and biomass-at-age, total biomass and SSB, and age-1 recruitment through 2019. Fleet F is shown by annual figures; full annual F-at-age arrays and associated uncertainty were not recovered.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation. SEDAR 71 is the latest completed operational assessment located for this distinct South Atlantic unit, with terminal year 2019. Its report supplies the core annual catch and aggregate index series, fleet age-composition figures, numeric age-specific outputs, and biological inputs. Catch-at-age requires a documented reconstruction from totals and figure-digitized compositions. The planned SEDAR 106 assessment (terminal year 2024) was delayed and has no replacement schedule posted as of the review date, so it is not a completed run to substitute.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART row 10349 is the South Atlantic Gag Grouper unit and is distinct from Gulf Gag Grouper (Stock SMART row 10348; candidate unit noaa_gag_gulf). The 2021 SEDAR report is a production operational assessment; SEDAR 106 is a delayed, in-progress successor. Sources are cached under the ignored source_cache/noaa_gag_sedar71_2021/ directory with URL and checksum provenance.

catch_age_evidence: The accepted 2014 production assessment (data through 2010) fits commercial catch-at-length, not observed annual catch-at-age. The April 2026 preliminary update reports port-sampled age material from 1991-2012, but says age compositions will first be compared as marginal data and considered for the likelihood only after representativeness checks; numerical annual age frequencies were not recovered.
survey_age_evidence: The 2014 assessment uses an aggregate fishery-dependent CPUE index. The 2026 update states that wreckfish are not regularly caught by NOAA surveys and there is no fishery-independent survey index; its commercial LPUE index is aggregate, with no age-specific abundance series.
weights_evidence: The 2014 model derives weight-at-age from a growth curve and length-weight relationship. The 2026 preliminary report supplies growth and length-weight parameters, but the current length-only base fit does not provide a complete annual observed weight-at-age input matrix.
maturity_evidence: The 2014 assessment models maturity at length and converts it to age through the age-length distribution. The 2026 report lists length-based maturity parameters; no annual observed maturity-at-age input series was located.
mortality_evidence: The 2014 reference case estimates age-independent M (0.0366 per year); the 2026 preliminary model uses life-history M of 0.037 per year with SD 0.00407. The April 2026 SSC report notes that M is not estimable from the available data. No annual age-specific M surface was reported.
timing_evidence: The abundance inputs are aggregate annual fishery-dependent indices, not seasonally timed survey series. Wreckfish commercial fishing years run April 15-January 15, but a fractional-year observation timing for the CPUE likelihood was not specified.
output_evidence: The accepted 2014 assessment reports stock biomass, recruitment, fishing mortality and reference-point outputs. The 2026 preliminary length-only model reports SSB with 95% confidence intervals and aggregate F/recruitment trends, but remains under development and is not the production assessment NOAA cites for current status.
decision_reason: Eligibility remains unresolved for the age-disaggregated expansion. The latest accepted production run fits catch-at-length and an aggregate CPUE index. The 2026 preliminary update identifies fishery age samples from 1991-2012, but says they have not yet been validated as representative or entered into the assessment likelihood; complete numerical age compositions and a final accepted current run were not located. Revisit if the age frequencies or final model files become public.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10369 has no canonical database match. NOAA still cites the 2014 assessment for status; SAFMC described the 2026 assessment as preliminary and under development. The 2026 working update is documented separately and does not replace the accepted production-run identity. Discovery screen only; no canonical values were imported.

catch_age_evidence: The latest SEDAR 92 production-era sources (data through 2023) use removals in weight, aggregate abundance indices for the southern ASPIC assessment, and, in the replacement DLM analysis, removals, length compositions, and life-history quantities. Neither model uses catch numbers-at-age or a fishery age-composition likelihood. Age-based life-history parameters do not constitute age-disaggregated catch inputs.
survey_age_evidence: SEDAR 92 uses aggregate CPUE indices in the southern ASPIC assessment. The May 2025 southern DLM analysis does not use an age-specific survey index; the northern DLM report states that no valid age compositions or abundance indices were available north of Cape Hatteras.
weights_evidence: The southern DLM uses a weight-length relationship, not an observed weights-at-age series. No run-specific weights-at-age likelihood input was identified for the 2025 assessment.
maturity_evidence: The DLM uses length at 50% maturity as a life-history input; the assessment does not use a maturity-at-age series in an age-structured population model.
mortality_evidence: The southern DLM uses a scalar natural mortality input (M = 0.17 with CV 0.24) based on maximum age and the Then et al. relationship. It is not a fitted age-specific M process.
timing_evidence: The 2025 DLM analyses use removals and broad length summaries; the sources do not specify a fractional timing for an age-specific survey observation. The earlier ASPIC model uses aggregate CPUE series.
output_evidence: SEDAR 92 reports aggregate biomass and fishing-mortality results from the southern ASPIC analysis, but the April 2025 SSC rejected that model as inadequate for management. The replacement DLM reports TAC distributions, not population-at-age or F-at-age outputs. NOAA still cites the 2017 assessment for South Atlantic stock-status estimates.
decision_reason: Ineligible for the age-disaggregated source set. NOAA Stock SMART lists the 2025 SEDAR 92 ASPIC run (assessment 13944, terminal year 2023) as rejected because its results were too uncertain. The South Atlantic SSC did not recommend the age-aggregated ASPIC model for management and supported average-catch DLM methods. The May 2025 DLM addendum documents removals, length compositions, life history, and TAC distributions, with no age-structured observations or population outputs. The latest accepted 2017 South Atlantic run was also ASPIC. The assessment unit has no verified age-disaggregated likelihood inputs.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10381 is a distinct South Atlantic management unit; its species page continues to identify the 2017 assessment for stock status. SEDAR 92 covers the broader Atlantic stock and separates regions at Cape Hatteras. Keep this NOAA unit distinct from the separate Mid- Atlantic Stock SMART unit; do not treat the shared SEDAR report as proof that the two management units are identical. Run metadata come from the 2026-10-28 cached Stock SMART inventory.

catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 22 used landings, length compositions, and age compositions conditional on 2-cm length bin. Appendix B reports year, length bin, sample size and counts at ages 2-30+ by fishery/survey and region; the assessment age data are not direct catch numbers-at-age. Catch-at-age can be reconstructed from these age-at-length counts, matching length compositions and removals, with the reconstruction documented as approximate.
survey_age_evidence: The model fits commercial longline and NMFS bottom-longline survey indices for east and west Gulf regions. NMFS survey age compositions are provided conditional on length in Appendix B, so age-specific survey values can be reconstructed by combining the index with the matched length-age samples; the report does not supply a direct age-specific abundance index.
weights_evidence: The assessment fixed its weight-length and region/gender growth inputs from the SEDAR 22 Data Workshop life-history sources. DW-01 reports observed size-at-age and growth information; a model-compatible weight-at-age surface can be reproduced from the documented growth and weight-length inputs.
maturity_evidence: The model fixed the maturity schedule from the Data Workshop. The assessment report gives a female age-maturity logistic with 50% maturity at age 2 and uses gonad weight for its spawning-biomass output; preserve this biological definition rather than treating it as ordinary mature somatic biomass.
mortality_evidence: The central SS run fixes the reference M parameter at 0.137 at age 4 and uses region- and gender-specific Lorenzen curves derived from growth. Alternative M assumptions were explored in sensitivity runs.
timing_evidence: The fitted indices are annual commercial and NMFS bottom-longline series. The reviewed assessment sources do not specify a fractional within-year observation time for the indices.
output_evidence: SEDAR 22 Table 3.7 reports annual east, west and Gulf total biomass and gonad-weight spawning biomass, age-0 recruitment and fishing mortality for the central SS run. These are aggregate model outputs; numeric annual N-at-age and F-at-age surfaces were not located in the reviewed report.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation: the latest detailed official assessment has age-composition counts by year and length bin, matched length compositions, annual removals, biology and aggregate population/mortality outputs, so age-specific inputs are reconstructable with an explicit length-age expansion. Keep the severe advice limitation prominent: NOAA Stock SMART records only partial acceptance for status determinations; the Gulf SSC said the model did not capture stock dynamics well enough for useful advice, and the OFL/ABC advice was based on historical landings. Age-based model outputs are therefore a cautious comparison reference, not an endorsed quantitative advice series.
notes: NOAA identifies Gulf, South Atlantic and Mid-Atlantic golden tilefish as separate management units; no canonical Gulf tilefish record exists. Stock SMART assessment 3057 is the latest run used for Gulf status, with data through 2009 and review result Partial acceptance - Status determinations only. NOAA and SEDAR list 2026 SEFSC01 work as data triage and preliminary composition documentation, not a completed replacement assessment. Do not mix those 2026 data with SEDAR 22 inputs. Discovery screen only; no canonical values were imported.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 SEDAR 89 Rev2 BAM uses fleet removals and age compositions for commercial handline and longline, with modeled ages 1-20+; recreational landings are also included. SEDAR89-WP-06 documents commercial age and length-composition construction. Sample sizes and observed/fitted fleet composition figures are reported; some annual matrices need digitization.
survey_age_evidence: The BAM fits aggregate commercial longline and fishery-independent MARMAP longline abundance indices. MARMAP age compositions are also used; the report provides sample sizes and observed/fitted composition figures. No directly age-specific abundance index was identified.
weights_evidence: SEDAR 89 Table 6 reports age-specific whole and gutted weights for model ages 1-20+, alongside length, sex ratio, maturity, egg production and M.
maturity_evidence: SEDAR89-WP-03 documents reproductive sampling and maturity modeling. The assessment converts female maturity-at-length to age and reports age-specific maturity and egg production in Table 6.
mortality_evidence: The base model uses fixed age-specific M, with the Lorenzen M-at-age relationship described in the report and numeric values in Table 6. Natural-mortality uncertainty is also represented in the MCBE ensemble.
timing_evidence: The model is annual, with numbers-at-age at the start of year and SSB at peak spawning (15 May, 0.37 year). The annual MARMAP index does not state a fractional observation time; verify this detail rather than assigning the spawning date to the survey.
output_evidence: Tables 7-8 report annual abundance-at-age (1000 fish) and biomass-at-age (mt) for 1972-2022; Table 10 reports annual SSB, recruitment and apical F. MCBE outputs provide uncertainty for derived assessment quantities.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation as a distinct new NOAA South Atlantic unit. NOAA Stock SMART identifies the latest accepted BAM run as assessment 14290 (2025; terminal year 2022). The public report and SEDAR89-WP-06 document age compositions, catch/abundance inputs and age-specific biology; the report includes numeric N-at-age and annual outputs. Age-composition matrices need source extraction/digitization, and MARMAP fractional observation timing remains to be verified. This is a source screen only; no canonical assessment data are created.
notes: Keep separate from NOAA:10385 Mid-Atlantic and NOAA:10383 Gulf units. NOAA identifies three management stocks; the South Atlantic assessment uses its own regional unit. SEDAR 89 Rev2 describes data through 2022 and uses ages 1-20+.

catch_age_evidence: The 2024 management-track WHAM assessment uses commercial catch and catch age compositions for ages 1-10+, with an age-length key developed for 2009 onward and earlier pooled keys. Commercial discards and recreational landings were added. SASINF input figures show the annual catch-composition series; exact arrays need digitization or file recovery.
survey_age_evidence: No fishery-independent abundance index is included in the 2024 model. The assessment uses annual commercial longline CPUE indices; SASINF shows three aggregate index series. Catch age compositions provide age data, but index and catch matrices are published mainly as figures.
weights_evidence: The SASINF final input report shows annual age-specific weights for SSB, January 1 biomass, catch and each fleet/index, for ages 1-10+. The public values are chart-based and require extraction.
maturity_evidence: The SASINF final input report plots the maturity-at-age schedule for ages 1-10+. The exact vector is not tabulated in the reviewed files.
mortality_evidence: Age-specific natural mortality is shown for ages 1-10+ in the final WHAM input report. The review discusses age-dependent M as a sensitivity; exact vector construction and values need extraction during curation.
timing_evidence: The model uses annual commercial CPUE indices and no fishery-independent survey index, so no separate within-year survey fraction is reported. Preserve the annual index convention and document any timing approximation
output_evidence: The assessment summary reports SSB (mt), fully selected F at age 6, and age-1 recruitment (thousands) for 2014-2023. SASINF final results show N-at-age, SSB-at-age, F and recruitment trajectories; aggregate output CVs are plotted.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation as a distinct new NOAA Mid-Atlantic unit. Stock SMART identifies the 2024 WHAM assessment (assessment 13544, terminal year 2023) as fully accepted. The peer-review panel found it technically sufficient and BSIA for management. NOAA SASINF exposes final input and results reports with age-structured data and population outputs for ages 1-10+. Most source series are chart-based and require digitization; the public report remains labeled draft, a publication-status caveat.
notes: Keep separate from South Atlantic NOAA:10384. The 2024 peer-review report confirms the management-track run was used for advice, with data through 2023. The SASINF archive contains reports and graphics rather than a native fitted model/data object; exact input arrays need recovery.

catch_age_evidence: The accepted 2025 WHAM update reports annual commercial and recreational catch totals and plots age-composition proportions by fishery for ages 0-5 and 6+ over 1985-2024. Catch-at-age can be reconstructed as each fishery total multiplied by its plotted age proportions; source values require figure digitization, and the exact sample-size series is not in the SASINF bundle.
survey_age_evidence: The input report plots nine aggregate index series and age compositions for age-sampled indices on the 0-5 and 6+ grid. Index trends are shown rescaled, so only relative series can be recovered from the plotted values without the source arrays; age-indexed values can be reconstructed from those series and digitized compositions with index-specific q.
weights_evidence: Annual weight-at-age surfaces for the stock, commercial and recreational fleets, and survey series are plotted for ages 0-5 and 6+. Numeric matrices are not included in the bundle and require digitization or recovery from survey/fishery source files.
maturity_evidence: The production input report plots a maturity-at-age schedule for ages 0-5 and 6+; the numeric schedule is not tabulated in the bundle.
mortality_evidence: The accepted 2022 research-track WHAM assessment replaced constant M=0.2 with age-varying Lorenzen weight-based M. The 2025 update reports using recent-year M averages for projections, but does not include its run-specific M vector or input code; carry-forward of the 2022 method should be verified during source curation.
timing_evidence: The 2025 WHAM assessment is annual and its input bundle does not record fractional-year observation times. The index names identify the survey series, but tinyAM translation will need survey-season timing from the underlying survey documentation and must label any annualization as an approximation.
output_evidence: The 2025 fitted parameter tables report numeric abundance-at-age in thousands and total and fleet fishing mortality-at-age for ages 0-5 and 6+, annually from 1985-2024. The report also gives aggregate catch/status outputs, including SSB and age-0 recruitment. Uncertainty for each annual age-specific output cell is not reported in these tables.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation as a new NOAA Atlantic Coast unit. Stock SMART identifies assessment 13933 (2025, data through 2024, WHAM, full acceptance), and the final peer-review panel concluded the assessment met all terms of reference and represented best scientific information available. The accepted input report contains plotted fleet and survey age compositions, relative abundance indices, age-specific weights and maturity; catch totals are reported and age-specific N/F outputs are numeric. These inputs are source-recoverable by digitization or documented reconstruction, but are not ready for direct numeric import.
notes: The 2025 SASINF archive contains report, plot, and fitted-table PDFs, but no run-specific WHAM input file or model code. Figure input pages use bubble areas to show age proportions; only the survey index trends are rescaled. The 2022 research-track report and WP06 document the Lorenzen M method; confirm that the 2025 update retained the same production-run M assumptions. Exact composition sample sizes and fractional survey timing were not found. This screen adds no canonical database values.

catch_age_evidence: The 2020 official update fits recreational conditional age-at-length compositions, ages 0-10 with age 10 as a plus group. The report records 1,266 age-length samples in 1987-2002 and 2004-2018 (none in 2003). It does not fit direct catch-at-age. Annual recreational length compositions and landings are published, so a documented reconstruction is possible in principle; the numerical conditional age compositions are plotted rather than tabulated, and no native SS3 input files were linked.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment uses aggregate fishery-dependent abundance indices: MRIP for 1981-2018 and SRHS headboat for 1986-2019. Both use selectivity matching the aggregate recreational fleet. Age-at-length observations come from recreational fishery samples; there is no separate age-specific survey index. Any index-at-age reconstruction would therefore be an approximation and must retain that distinction.
weights_evidence: The report provides the fixed sex-combined length-weight relationship and sex-specific growth inputs. Weight-at-age can be derived from those official inputs; it is not a directly observed annual age-specific weight surface.
maturity_evidence: Maturity is fixed by age: age 2 is 50% mature and ages 3+ are fully mature. The model uses a 60% female sex ratio.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed as an age-specific scaled Lorenzen vector, with fully selected-age M = 0.38 per year; no M process is estimated.
timing_evidence: The model is annual and assumes fishing and spawning occur continuously and homogeneously through the year; no within-year survey timing fraction is specified.
output_evidence: Table 15 reports annual model biomass, SSB, total abundance, age-0 recruitment and depletion for 1927-2018. Recruitment uncertainty is also plotted. Numbers-at-age are shown graphically; a numerical N-at-age table was not located. The report includes fleet mortality/selectivity graphics, but no numerical F-at-age table was located.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation: the official update is age structured, includes conditional age-at-length observations, annual catch and abundance inputs, fixed age-specific biology, and reported population outputs. The age composition values are available in figures rather than machine-readable tables, so import readiness depends on recovering or transparently digitizing and validating those inputs.
notes: Latest detailed Gulf assessment located is the SEDAR 28 update dated June 2020, with data through 2018; the 2024 NOAA management amendment continues to rely on this assessment. Keep this Gulf unit separate from Southern Atlantic cobia. The assessment report notes low confidence and data limitations, including poor fit to age compositions and uncertain abundance-index interpretation.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 single-area, two-sex Stock Synthesis model uses annual catch biomass in metric tonnes for three fisheries: commercial, at-sea hake, and recreational. The input bundle includes fishery age and length compositions, including age-at-length data. Catch-at-age is not a direct annual observation series and would require reconstruction from catch totals and age compositions.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses four survey indices: Oregon-Washington hook-and-line (numbers), Triennial and WCGBTS (biomass), and SMURF (recruitment index). Triennial age and length data and WCGBTS conditional age-at-length data are included. An age-specific abundance index is not a direct input and would require an explicit index-composition reconstruction.
weights_evidence: Sex-specific weight-at-age is derived from the fitted sex-specific growth curves and estimated weight-at-length relationships; the report and native output describe the resulting age surfaces.
maturity_evidence: Female age-based maturity is estimated from 232 histological samples of aged fish collected north of 40.167 degrees N during 2016-2023.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is estimated freely with a lognormal prior based on maximum age; the prior uses age 43, the 99.9th percentile of PacFIN age observations.
timing_evidence: The native input records month 7 (July) for its survey index series and month 7 for the Triennial and WCGBTS age observations. The model spawning month is January. Preserve the observation month in any fractional-year conversion.
output_evidence: The native Report.sso includes annual numbers-at-age, catch-at-age, biomass-at-age, F-at-age, recruitment, and spawning output. The report provides uncertainty for key population quantities.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10393 is the U.S. northern yellowtail stock north of 40 degrees 10 minutes N. It is distinct from the Canadian coastwide DFO unit and has no matching canonical stock. The adopted 2025 benchmark assessment has matching native inputs and outputs with fishery and survey age data, age-specific biology, and fitted age surfaces. Mark eligible for source curation and documented age-structured approximation; direct catch-at-age and age-specific survey indices are not observed likelihood inputs.
notes: The official unit is northern yellowtail rockfish north of 40 degrees 10 minutes N. The 2025 single-area assessment is sex-specific, uses 40 population ages and age-composition bins 1-30, and data through 2024. The report and model bundle identify Stock Synthesis 3.30.23.1. The report and native ZIP, retrieval details, and checksums are in source_cache/discovery_noaa_yellowtail_2025/sources.csv.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 Stock Synthesis input has retained catch biomass (metric tonnes) for trawl, hook-and-line and pot fleets, plus discard fleets. weights_evidence: The assessment reads sex-specific empirical weight-at-age inputs from WCGBTS biological samples for ages 0-30 in 2003-2024 (age 30 is the plus group); pre-2003 weights are held constant.

mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is estimated as one time-invariant value shared by sexes: 0.088 per year in the base model, with a lognormal prior having median 0.072 and standard error 0.31.
timing_evidence: The native survey observations include month fields. catch_age_evidence: The 2024 m22.5a full assessment fits total catch biomass in metric tonnes for 1977-2024 and fishery age compositions. The data summary lists fishery age-composition years 1998-2002, 2004-2006, 2008-2020 (biennial), and 2022; the report describes sampled fish aged 4-66. Annual catch-at-age numbers are not a native input, but source catch biomass, age proportions, and weight-at-age support a documented reconstruction. The report contains a discrepancy between the model data-year summary and the narrative sample years that needs checking during curation.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses GOA bottom-trawl VAST biomass estimates (tonnes, with standard errors and confidence intervals) for 1990-2023 and survey age compositions for 1990-2023. Survey age compositions are proportions for ages 4-29 plus a 30+ group, with input/effective sample sizes and haul counts. Biomass, age proportions, and weights-at-age permit documented age-specific index reconstruction; the report does not provide an age-specific biomass index directly.
weights_evidence: Mean weight-at-age is estimated outside the model from survey size-at-age data for combined sexes. The SAFE gives a weight growth equation in grams with W-infinity=1928 g, kappa=0.190, t0=0.607, and exponent b=3.0, supporting a documented age-specific weight reconstruction.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity-at-age is represented by a logistic curve estimated conditionally from combined observations cited to Lunsford (1997, personal communication) and Chilton (2010); the assessment fits female maturity-at-age conditionally with a logistic curve and binomial likelihood using combined observations cited to Lunsford (1997, personal communication) and Chilton (2010); reported age at 50% maturity is 10.3. The SAFE shows the curve but does not tabulate the combined raw observations or the full coefficient pair, which must be recovered or documented before import.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed at M=0.07 per year throughout the assessment; it is not estimated by age. The SAFE explains the historical basis and notes estimates from maximum observed ages.
timing_evidence: The assessment uses annual trawl-survey biomass and age-composition observations, but does not report a fractional within-year survey timing. Survey timing remains unresolved for any translation requiring a timing fraction.
output_evidence: The 2024 SAFE reports annual MLE female spawning biomass, total age-4+ biomass, fully selected F, and age-4 recruitment, plus MCMC means and 95% credible intervals for those time series. It does not provide numerical N-at-age or F-at-age surfaces. The September 2026 pre-dissemination peer-review harvest projection updates catch and projected biomass, but explicitly reruns no assessment model and is not formally disseminated by NMFS.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation. assessment_area: Central subpopulation, California to northern Baja California; Stock SMART label: Southern Pacific Coast
catch_age_evidence: The native SS input contains 2000-2021 semester catches in metric tonnes for two pooled MexCal fleets and their age-composition proportions. These are not direct catch numbers-at-age; the report documents reconstructing them from monthly landings, age proportions and final weight-at-age, then aggregating to semesters.
survey_age_evidence: The base model fits acoustic-trawl summer and spring biomass indices with lognormal errors; the run archive includes survey age compositions and weights-at-age. Age-specific survey abundance is reconstructable from index biomass, age composition and weight-at-age, but is not a direct age-specific index likelihood.
weights_evidence: The native weight-at-age file contains empirical fleet-, year- and semester-specific weights for ages 0, 1, 2 and 3+. The report documents averaging and interpolation used for missing fishery values; survey values were derived from acoustic-trawl age and length data.
maturity_evidence: Fixed maturity proportions are approximately 0.726, 0.931, 0.985 and 0.997 for ages 0, 1, 2 and 3+; fecundity is fixed at one gram of eggs per gram body weight.
mortality_evidence: The base model estimates uniform natural mortality; the report gives 0.414 per year. Steepness is fixed at 0.6.
timing_evidence: The model runs 2015-2021 in biological semesters: June-December (7 months) and January-May (5 months), with a June 1 birth date. The run file records a survey timing field and assigns observations to semesters; an unambiguous within-semester calendar fraction was not recovered.
output_evidence: Tables 11-14 report numbers-at-age (thousands of fish), biomass-at-age and annual biomass (metric tonnes), SSB and recruitment with asymptotic standard errors; the report also gives the 0.414 per-year M estimate. Apical F by fishery is plotted, not tabulated by age.
decision_reason: The latest detailed production assessment located is the 2021 CSNA benchmark adopted in 2022. Its native run archive supplies fishery and survey age compositions, catches, weights and fixed maturity; the report supplies age-structured population outputs. Catch-at-age and an age-specific survey index can be reconstructed using the report-documented transformations, so the unit is eligible for source curation. No numerical data have been imported.
notes: Stock SMART 10574 uses “Southern Pacific Coast”; the PFMC run calls this the central subpopulation. The current NOAA page identifies the southern stock as assessed in 2022. The historical Charbonneau-Keith E. mordax label is actually Iberian E. encrasicolus and is not a match. See source_reviews/noaa_northern_anchovy_central_subpopulation_2021.md.

stock_name: Coho salmon - Oregon Production Index Area: Central California Coast

catch_age_evidence: Stock SMART classifies the 2026 assessment as "Cohort Analysis" (Model Category 2, Composition Input Data 0). weights_evidence: The reviewed 2026 production report and coho FRAM documentation do not provide weights-at-age for a multi-age assessment. The operational model tracks only age-3 adults.
maturity_evidence: The reviewed 2026 production report and coho FRAM documentation do not provide maturity-at-age for a multi-age assessment. The operational model tracks only age-3 adults.
mortality_evidence: Coho FRAM calculates natural and fishery mortality across five within-year time steps for the single age-3 cohort; natural mortality is common across stocks and years. Published exploitation/mortality outputs are fishery-specific and not multi-age F-at-age or M-at-age series.
timing_evidence: FRAM has five within-year fishery time steps (Jan-Jun, July, August, September, Oct-Dec), but the 2026 assessment has no age-specific survey likelihood with a survey sampling-time parameter.
output_evidence: The 2026 PFMC report provides no Central California Coast coho age-structured population series; Stock SMART reports no time series for this unit. Published adult ocean abundance/run-size outputs are commonly expressed in thousands of age-3 fish; they are not N-at-age surfaces spanning multiple ages.
decision_reason: Ineligible for the age-disaggregated assessment set. The latest operational record is the 2026 Coho assessment using data through 2025. The accessible 2026 PFMC report and joint FRAM documentation describe annual forecasting and fishery accounting for one adult age class (age 3), not the multi-age population process and inputs required for tinyAM. Some Stock SMART metadata indicate size/age composition data were used, but no multi-age likelihood vectors or population surfaces are published. The FRAM run database and supporting files are password-protected; their absence from public sources is recorded as a source limitation, not proof that underlying biological samples do not exist.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART stock ID 10581 is a distinct U.S. coho management unit (Oncorhynchus kisutch), not a one-to-one match to the DFO Interior Fraser or North Coast coho candidates. Several NOAA forecast components share a broader OPI or regional forecast and remain distinct inventory units. Source PDFs and FRAM documentation are cached under source_cache/discovery_noaa_coho_2026/sources.csv with retrieval dates and SHA-256 checksums. FRAM documentation states only age-3 fish are modeled; annual run database files are hosted in a password-protected NWIFC section. No canonical assessment or numerical records were added.

stock_name: Alaska skate - Bering Sea / Aleutian Islands
catch_age_evidence: The 2023 operational Model 14.2d uses aggregate reconstructed catch by longline and trawl, including gear-specific catch-accounting estimates. Its Stock Synthesis file has no fishery age-composition records; catch units are biomass, not numbers-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment fits an EBS shelf survey biomass index and survey length compositions. Paired survey length-at-age observations occur only in 2003, 2007-2009, and 2015 and inform the growth curve; they are not age compositions or an age-specific abundance index. The report states there are no fishery ages and no new survey age data since the prior full assessment.
weights_evidence: The model uses a combined-sex length-weight relationship (weight in kg, total length in cm): W = 9.0e-6 * TL^2.9617. No observed weight-at-age input is reported; an age surface would require derivation from this relationship and fitted growth.
maturity_evidence: Maturity is modeled as a length-based ogive (L50 = 93.28 cm total length; slope = -0.548). No observed maturity-at-age input is reported; an age surface would require derivation using fitted growth.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed at M = 0.13 per year for Alaska skate; the Other Skates Tier 5 unit is separate and uses M = 0.10.
timing_evidence: The one-season Stock Synthesis input uses survey observations in month 7 and spawning month 1. This is a calendar-month specification; no separate fractional-year survey timing input was reported.
output_evidence: The 2023 Model 14.2d output archive reports N-at-age for ages 0-25 and years 1948-2028 (unit not stated in the CSV), biomass in metric tonnes, age-0 recruitment in thousands of fish with CV, and aggregate exploitation (catch / total biomass). The report also provides age-structured population output, but these fitted quantities do not replace missing age-disaggregated observations. No comparable F-at-age or M-at-age summary table was located.
decision_reason: The latest completed operational assessment located is the 2023 Model 14.2d, used for 2024 harvest specifications. It has aggregate catch and survey-biomass observations with length compositions, but no fishery age compositions or age-specific abundance observations. The sparse survey length-at-age samples inform growth only. Therefore it is ineligible for the age-disaggregated source set despite age-structured fitted outputs.
notes: This candidate is the Tier 3 BSAI Alaska skate component; the BSAI Other Skates Tier 5 complex is a separate assessment unit. The NOAA Stock SMART Gulf of Alaska Skate Complex (NOAA:11005) is also separate and was not matched to this unit. The 2024 SAFE is a harvest projection, while the 2025 alternatives were proposals rather than an accepted production assessment. NPFMC scheduled the 2026 BSAI skates final assessment for December 2026, after this review date. The cached 2023 SS3 data file is under the Model 14.2d update path and has _EndYr=2023, but its header comment still says data through 2020; run identity is supported by the official report and output files, and this stale comment is retained as a provenance caveat. No canonical records were added and no tinyAM translation was attempted.

stock_name: Northern rock sole - Gulf of Alaska
catch_age_evidence: The 2021 full assessment used annual total rock sole catch, split evenly between northern and southern rock sole; fishery composition inputs were length compositions (1997-2021), not catch-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The NMFS GOA bottom-trawl survey supplied biomass and length compositions plus conditional age-at-length data. Northern rock sole CAAL samples are documented through 2017; the report states 2019 ages were unavailable for this species.
weights_evidence: The report describes a shared length-weight relationship; no complete numeric weight-at-age series was recovered.
maturity_evidence: Age-based maturity is a fixed model input shown graphically; the numeric vector was not recovered.
mortality_evidence: For preferred 2021 northern rock sole Model 21.2, female M was fixed at 0.2; male M was estimated at 0.232 centrally and 0.254 in the west.
timing_evidence: The report describes GOA groundfish survey years and spawning seasons, but does not provide exact timing proportions for tinyAM.
output_evidence: The 2021 full report and later Stock SMART monitoring rows provide biomass, SSB, M, and harvest-reference outputs. Annual full N-at-age and F-at-age arrays were not recovered; the 2025 SAFE catch report says no assessment was run in 2025.
decision_reason: Not eligible for the current tinyAM age-structured translation screen: the documented official model uses annual total catch split by species and fishery length compositions, not catch-at-age. Survey biomass and conditional age-at-length data do not provide the missing fishery age composition. The numeric age-specific biology and N/F-at-age output arrays were not recovered from the report sources.
