assessment_area: Southern Atlantic Coast / Gulf of Mexico
catch_age_evidence: The accepted 2025 operational SEDAR 96 assessment is an age- and size-structured Stock Synthesis model, ages 0-20. It reports age compositions for headboat and MRIP landings during 1981-2023, raised with annual landings to weighted landings-at-age; commercial ages from 1992-2023 are configured as conditional age-at-length data. The numerical compositions are shown in figures, and the reviewed public files did not include the model-ready input vectors.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses four aggregate abundance indices (commercial CPUE, MRIP CPUE, Reef Fish Visual Census Florida Keys, and Dry Tortugas). RVC index compositions are length-based; the additional fishery-independent conditional age-at-length data are not linked to an index. The public materials therefore do not verify an index-specific age distribution for reconstructing the RVC series at age.
weights_evidence: The assessment uses a fixed length-weight relationship, weight = 2.574e-5 * fork_length_cm^2.8797, and estimated growth within Stock Synthesis. Model weight-at-age is consequently derived within the model; a numeric weight-at-age input vector was not found in the public document bundle.
maturity_evidence: Maturity-at-age is fixed using the schedule adopted in SEDAR 64: 50% mature at age 1.7 and all mature by age 4, extended through age 20. The 2025 report references the schedule but the reviewed public files do not include the model input vector.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality-at-age is fixed, constant through time, and derived from the Lorenzen relationship using the external growth model. The reviewed report describes the assumption but the public document bundle did not include the numeric model input vector.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual (January-December); surveys, compositions, and conditional age-at-length observations are configured at mid-year (July 1). The Dry Tortugas RVC index itself samples May-July in listed survey years.
output_evidence: The report says the fitted model estimates a full N-at-age time series (1,000s of fish), biomass, female SSB, age-0 recruitment, and fishing mortality. It tabulates annual total/SSB and recruitment and age-4/apical F, but the exact N-at-age surface is not provided as a numerical table or native model output in the reviewed public document bundle.
decision_reason: The latest official assessment found is the fully accepted 2025 SEDAR 96 operational assessment (data through 2023), which is genuinely age-structured and has age-based catch compositions, fixed biological assumptions, and age-specific population outputs. Eligibility remains unresolved for the age-disaggregated comparison: the public bundle does not contain model-ready annual age vectors, the fishery-independent indices have length rather than index-specific age compositions, and the numerical N-at-age surface is not published as a table or native output file. Do not construct age-specific survey observations or population outputs from unrelated compositions or figures without recovering and documenting the underlying data.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART ID 11081 is the single Southeastern U.S. Yellowtail Snapper management stock shared by South Atlantic and Gulf councils; SEDAR 96 models one Florida population area and ages 0-20. catch_age_evidence: The 2025 single-area, two-sex model covers the combined Rougheye and Blackspotted management complex. It uses catch biomass in metric tonnes for six fisheries and conditional age-at-length (CAAL) observations from fishery sampling. CAAL data enter the likelihood; marginal age compositions are supplied for fit evaluation. Catch-at-age is not a direct annual input and would require reconstruction from catches and sampled age information.
survey_age_evidence: The native model includes indices for Triennial, Alaska slope, Northwest slope, and WCGBTS surveys, with survey age/length observations described in the report. The data file retains survey observation timing and age compositions. An age-specific abundance index is not a direct model input and would require a documented reconstruction from aggregate indices and age compositions.
weights_evidence: The model derives weight-at-age from its fitted growth and weight-at-length parameters; the native Report.sso includes biomass-at-age output.
maturity_evidence: The model uses a length-based maturity relationship documented in the 2025 report; age-specific maturity can be derived from the model growth surface if required for a tinyAM approximation.
mortality_evidence: Female natural mortality is estimated. Male natural mortality is fixed at 0.036 per year following likelihood-profile analysis; alternative M values are used in the report uncertainty scenarios.
timing_evidence: The native data file records observation months for survey series and the model has January spawning. Preserve each observation month when converting to fractional-year survey timing.
output_evidence: The native Report.sso includes annual numbers-at-age, catch-at-age, biomass-at-age, F-at-age and natural-mortality outputs. The report provides spawning output, recruitment and management quantities with uncertainty.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 14516 is the U.S. West Coast Rougheye/Blackspotted management complex, consisting of Sebastes aleutianus and Sebastes melanostictus treated as one assessment unit. No matching canonical stock record was found. The adopted 2025 assessment has a matching native Stock Synthesis bundle with catch totals, CAAL and survey age data, biological assumptions, and fitted age-specific outputs. Mark eligible for source curation and an explicitly approximate age-structured translation; it is one complex and must not be counted as two cases.
notes: The report covers U.S. waters from the U.S.-Canada border to the U.S.-Mexico border and treats the two species as one management complex because they are difficult to distinguish in catches. The model uses data through 2024, two sexes, 140 population ages, and one area. The report and native bundle identify Stock Synthesis 3.30.23.2. Cached sources and checksums are listed in source_cache/discovery_noaa_rougheye_2025/sources.csv.

catch_age_evidence: IPHC-2026-TSD-031 provides directed-fishery age-frequency specimen counts by regulatory area, year (1993-2025), and sex; the 2026-06 table revision is later than the assessment vintage and 2025 is preliminary. survey_age_evidence: Public IPHC FISS individual records cover 1998-2025 and include age, sex, maturity, length, station, and year; 365,576 of 2,273,521 records have a resolved age. Splitting that index by observed age composition is possible for sampled area-years; unsampled areas are not extrapolated. weights_evidence: The 2025 assessment overview describes sex-, area-, age-, and year-specific FISS and fishery weight-at-age, with population values smoothed across years. These support a documented reconstruction, but the exact four-model input matrices are not in the public assessment bundle.
maturity_evidence: The 2025 assessment updated the female maturity ogive using histology from 2022-2024; the data overview reports a curve truncated below age 7. mortality_evidence: The 2025 ensemble includes four model structures: female natural mortality is estimated in three models and fixed at 0.15/year in the coastwide short model; male natural mortality is estimated in all four. Preserve model-specific M treatment rather than treating the ensemble as one fixed-M specification.
timing_evidence: The FISS is an annual summer survey conducted across late May-September; the assessment is annual. Sources establish a seasonal window but not one common within-year sampling fraction. Any single tinyAM timing would be an explicit approximation, ideally using area/year survey dates.

Public numeric historical N-at-age and F-at-age arrays were not found.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART 11082 and the DFO Pacific halibut inventory entry refer to the same IPHC Convention Area resource spanning Canada and the United States; neither maps to a canonical tinyAM stock, so these two inventory rows are one provisional new unit. Public commercial age frequencies, area-specific landings, FISS age samples, an area-specific FISS abundance index, biology, and annual SSB outputs support source-based age-input reconstruction, so the unit is eligible for source curation with explicit approximations. weights_evidence: Mean weight observations were used for U.S. and Canadian fleets; an age-specific weight-at-age series was not located in the reviewed assessment sources.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is fixed at 50% at age 5 and 100% at older ages; fecundity is related to body weight.

output_evidence: The 2022 assessment reports aggregate spawning-biomass and fishing-mortality status outputs. Annual numeric N-, F-, or M-at-age output arrays were not located.

assessment_area: West Coast Vancouver Island, Barkley Sound Stock Management Unit (three Conservation Units)
catch_age_evidence: The 2024 report says age and stock composition are used in annual run-size reconstruction for three Conservation Units. weights_evidence: No model weight-at-age input is reported. The reviewed response reports run abundance, escapement, harvest, exploitation rate, and recruits per spawner, not age-specific population biomass.
maturity_evidence: No maturity-at-age input is reported. Adult spawner counts and stock-recruit reference points do not provide an age-specific maturity vector for a marine population model.
mortality_evidence: The response reports exploitation rates and management targets, but no age-specific fishing-mortality surface or natural-mortality assumption for an age-structured population model.
timing_evidence: Run-timing curves inform in-season forecasting and management. There is no marine survey observation series requiring a survey timing fraction.
output_evidence: DFO Science Response 2026/022, the peer-reviewed update of the 2024 assessment, presents time series of harvest, escapement, exploitation rate, and recruits per spawner for the aggregate SMU and its three CUs, plus reference points with 80% credible intervals. It does not report annual N-at-age, F-at-age, or an age-structured biomass surface.
decision_reason: DFO identifies this as the latest 2024 Barkley Sockeye SMU assessment, but describes an index-based, stock-recruit, forecast, and run-reconstruction approach. assessment_area: NAFO Division 4T, southern Gulf of St. Lawrence
catch_age_evidence: The official age-structured assessment uses total annual fishery catch and fishery age compositions. Research Document 2025/008 Appendix Table A4 reports commercial catch-at-age in thousands for 1978-2022, with bins 0-2, ages 3-12 and 13+. The model grid is ages 2-10+, so age-bin mapping must be resolved and documented before import.
survey_age_evidence: The model likelihood uses age-aggregated RV and Mobile Sentinel biomass indices for ages 2-7 plus survey proportions-at-age. Appendix Table A5 also reports September RV stratified catch rates by age (fish/tow) for ages 2-14 and 1978-2022, which supports a documented age-indexed translation while preserving the native aggregate likelihood inputs.
weights_evidence: Age-specific weights from the fishery, RV and Mobile Sentinel surveys are identified as model inputs. Appendix Table A6 supplies RV mean weight-at-age in kg for 1978-2022; fishery and Mobile Sentinel numeric vectors still need recovery or verification before import.
maturity_evidence: The assessment assumes knife-edge maturity: ages 2-3 are immature and age 4 and older are fully mature.
mortality_evidence: The official model estimates independent natural-mortality time series for ages 2-3, 4-5 and 6+, with log-scale random-walk deviations.
timing_evidence: The RV survey is conducted in September and the Mobile Sentinel survey in August. The reports do not specify exact within-month fractions of year; any tinyAM timing values would be documented approximations.
output_evidence: The Science Advisory Report gives 2022 SSB as 6.1 kt and reports annual SSB, age-2 recruitment, age-6+ fishing mortality and age-group M trajectories. The detailed report describes MCMC-based intervals, but numeric annual uncertainty and N/F-at-age arrays were not recovered.
decision_reason: The official 2024 assessment is an age-structured model for the current DFO management unit, NAFO Division 4T, with source catch, survey age information, biological inputs, mortality assumptions and comparable population outputs. This is a distinct Canadian unit, not the existing NOAA Gulf of Maine/Georges Bank white hake stock. The directly reported age bins and non-RV weight vectors require further extraction before import.
notes: Assessment terminal year: 2022. The model covers 1978-2022 and ages 2-10+. Treat the age-specific RV catch-rate table as a reconstruction source, not as the assessment’s native likelihood (aggregate biomass plus age composition). Preserve native units and likelihood structure in the canonical database; translation remains unattempted.

assessment_area: NAFO Division 4T, southern Gulf of St. Lawrence
catch_age_evidence: The 2017 statistical catch-at-age assessment uses total commercial landings in tonnes and annual catch-at-age proportions for ages 2-12+ in numbers, 1973-2016 (Table 9). These source quantities support a documented number-at-age reconstruction using the annual fishery mean weights-at-age; they are not direct catch numbers-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The September RV survey provides annual trawlable biomass and survey abundance-at-age proportions for ages 2-12+, 1973-2016 (Table 10). Its age-specific index can be reconstructed from the biomass and survey weights-at-age. The model also used survey age proportions.
weights_evidence: Table 13 reports annual mean weights-at-age for the RV survey and fishery in kg per fish, ages 2-12+, 1973-2016.
maturity_evidence: Table 12 reports mature proportions-at-age for 1973-2016, derived from survey length-based maturity curves and the age-length key.
mortality_evidence: The statistical catch-at-age model estimates time-blocked natural mortality, with five-year blocks and either two age groups (2-4, 5+) or three (2-4, 5-7, 8+). M is not fixed.
timing_evidence: The model places the September RV survey at 0.71 of the annual time step. Fishery catches are annual totals; no separate within-year fishery observation fraction is used.
output_evidence: The assessment reports estimated SSB, age-2 and age-3 recruitment, fishing mortality, and time-varying M. Age-specific state surfaces are shown in figures, but no machine-readable run output or annual N-at-age table was located in the report.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation. The latest detailed full assessment located is the 2017 statistical catch-at-age model (Research Document 2019/026), with inputs for 1973-2016. The 2025/010 update is an interim survey-indicator update, not a new full assessment. Catch-at-age is reported as proportions and must be reconstructed from total catch and weights-at-age. The 2025 response says a full assessment is planned for 2026; check for its publication before importing. No canonical values have been added.
notes: Distinct from NOAA winter flounder units in Georges Bank, Gulf of Maine, and Southern New England/Mid-Atlantic. DFO identifies the current unit as NAFO Division 4T. The full report models one combined-sex population; its mixed catch-weight and composition inputs require documented conversions during extraction.

assessment_area: Gulf of St. Lawrence, NAFO Divisions 4RST
catch_age_evidence: The 2022 Research Document reports total landings by gear in tonnes for fishing years 1960-2021 and states the model uses the September-to-August series from 1961 onward. Commercial catch-at-length is described, but the fitted model is surplus production and does not use age-specific catch or length compositions.
survey_age_evidence: The model fits three aggregate trawlable-biomass indices for fish >=30 cm: the 4T September RV index (1971-1992), combined 4RST August/September RV index (1987-2021), and combined July/August sentinel index (2003-2019). An under-30-cm recruitment indicator is length-based. These are not age-specific abundance indices.
weights_evidence: No weight-at-age surface is used in the fitted model. The modeled state is biomass of fish >=30 cm; the report describes historical age samples for growth analysis, not an age-structured population or weight-at-age input.
maturity_evidence: The report estimates historical sex-specific maturity-at-age and maturity-at-length from survey biology, but these quantities are not inputs to the fitted surplus-production model. No annual age-specific maturity surface is used.
mortality_evidence: The fitted Schaefer model does not estimate or use age-specific natural mortality or fishing mortality. It estimates population growth, process variation, biomass and exploitation rate.
timing_evidence: The annual catch series is aligned from September of year t-1 to August of year t; model biomass is described as late-summer/early-fall biomass. The three indices combine August/September RV surveys or July/August sentinel surveys; no within-year age model
output_evidence: The official DFO dataset provides 30+ cm biomass posterior medians and 2.5th, 25th, 75th and 97.5th percentiles for 1961-2021 in tonnes, matching the 2022 report (2021 median about 17,768 t). The 2024 interim update extends a survey indicator through 2024, not the full model. No SSB, N-at-age or F-at-age trajectory is reported.
decision_reason: The latest full assessment is the 2022 Bayesian Schaefer surplus-production model to 2021. The 2024 update reports interim survey indicators and identifies a full assessment for 2027. Because the production model does not use age-disaggregated population or observation data, this unit is ineligible for the age-structured expansion batch.
notes: Confirmed as a distinct DFO Gulf unit (NAFO 4RST); not the separate US Gulf of Maine Witch Flounder record. No canonical database values were added. Full assessment: Ricard (2022), CSAS Research Document 2022/054; latest interim update covers 2024.

assessment_area: Groundfish Management Area 4B: Queen Charlotte Strait, Strait of Georgia, and Strait of Juan de Fuca
catch_age_evidence: The age-structured stock-reduction analyses used survey age compositions. The pinned source repository contains privacy-compliant sample objects and processing code.
survey_age_evidence: The 2021/008 report describes age data from area 4B surveys in 1984-2018, with most samples from the HBLL survey after it began in 2003. The SRA uses HBLL survey age compositions with an 80+ model group; sample sizes are small.
weights_evidence: Biological samples and growth relationships are documented, but a run-matched numeric weight-at-age input table was not verified in this screen.
maturity_evidence: The detailed rebuilding report derives age-based, sex-specific maturity ogives from survey biological samples.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is an assumed/distributional OM quantity informed by life history and prior work; the model does not estimate an age-specific M surface.
timing_evidence: The reports identify survey series and years, but a fractional within-year timing for the age-composition observations was not verified.
output_evidence: The latest detailed age-structured MSE report provides OM biomass trajectories and stock-status probabilities through 2019, not a standard annual N-at-age/F-at-age output table.
decision_reason: DFO identifies June 2020 as the latest science advice for the current inside unit. The detailed 2021/008 rebuilding analysis and its pinned source repository document age-structured SRA operating models and survey age-composition data. Eligibility remains unresolved for the age-disaggregated tinyAM candidate set because commercial age samples cover only one trip and do not establish annual catch-at-age; a numeric weight-at-age series, survey timing, and comparable age-specific outputs also remain unverified.

assessment_area: British Columbia outside waters; the 2026 advice reports a coastwide status update, with North and South operating-model components
catch_age_evidence: The detailed 2020/069 rebuilding analysis uses aggregate commercial catch and available age-composition inputs from commercial and survey sources. The 2024 update inputs could not be verified because its report PDF is currently unavailable at the official download URL.
survey_age_evidence: The 2019 age-structured operating models use survey age-composition data from PHMA, IPHC, and trawl sources. The 2023 update corrects the age- composition likelihood but explicitly adds no new data.
weights_evidence: The 2020/069 report documents growth and biological sampling, but a run-matched numeric weight-at-age input table for the 2024 update was not verified.
maturity_evidence: The 2020/069 operating models use age-based maturity derived from biological samples; the 2024 update-specific input was not verified.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is an uncertain operating-model quantity and was revised with the 2023 likelihood correction; it is not an estimated age-specific M surface.
timing_evidence: The 2020/069 report identifies the survey series, but the 2024 update report and its fractional survey timing could not be verified.
output_evidence: DFO published a 2026/039 science advisory report titled as a 2024 stock- status update. Its official PDF URL returned an archived-information placeholder during this review, so the current numeric outputs could not be checked. The 2023 advice reports status through 2018.
decision_reason: The current outside unit received a 2024 status update, published as DFO Science Advisory Report 2026/039 in August 2026. The official PDF link currently returns an archived-information page, so run-specific inputs and numerical outputs from the latest update remain unverified. Earlier same-unit documents confirm age-structured operating models and age- composition data, but cannot substitute for the current update. Keep eligibility unresolved pending access to the 2026 report and its detailed supporting data.
notes: The 2024 update is the primary current-unit record. The 2019 data through 2018 in Research Document 2020/069 and its 2023 likelihood correction are historical same-unit context only; they are not used to fill current-run gaps. Inside Yelloweye Rockfish remains a separate population. No canonical assessment or numeric series was imported.

catch_age_evidence: The 2021 Stock Synthesis assessment uses annual commercial catch estimates from 1935-2021 and commercial age-frequency samples from 28 years (1979-2019). Bottom and midwater trawl data are combined as one fishery. Quarterly age compositions were catch-weighted and expanded using quarterly landings; catch-at-age therefore requires a documented reconstruction. Numeric input matrices were not found as separate public files in this screen.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses four aggregate trawl biomass-index series (QCS, WCVI, WCHG, and GIG) covering 1967-2020 and survey age compositions from 25 years across the four surveys. Survey age data are downweighted to 0.25; aggregate indices and age compositions could support a documented age-index reconstruction.
weights_evidence: Sex-specific growth and length-weight relationships were estimated from survey biological samples and fixed over time. The report gives growth and allometric parameters needed to derive weight-at-age for model ages 1-60.
maturity_evidence: The model uses a time-invariant female maturity ogive: zero at ages 1-4, a fitted monotonic curve at ages 5-16, and 1.0 from age 17 through the age-60 accumulator. The source describes the biological samples and fitted form.
mortality_evidence: The composite base case pools five component runs with fixed scalar M values of 0.04, 0.045, 0.05, 0.055, and 0.06. An estimated-M sensitivity had poor MCMC diagnostics and is not the adopted central run. M is not age-specific.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. It defines spawning biomass at the start of the year and exploitation rate in mid-year. Exact fractional timing for each survey observation was not verified in the published report.
output_evidence: The official composite base case reports annual female spawning-biomass and age-0 recruitment trajectories with posterior intervals through 2022, plus tabulated terminal B2022 quantiles. Numeric N-at-age and instantaneous F-at-age arrays were not recovered; reported fishing pressure is exploitation.
decision_reason: DFO identifies the 2021 assessment as the latest detailed coastwide age-structured assessment found for this unit. The 2025/26 IFMP anticipated an update in 2024, but no later detailed Yellowmouth assessment was found in the current DFO Pacific plan or CSAS search. The 2021 report documents catch totals and age compositions, four survey indices and survey age data, biology, mortality scenarios, and official SSB/recruitment outputs. These support source curation with documented reconstruction; original numeric age matrices and exact survey timing remain source-recovery tasks.
notes: The assessment is coastwide across PMFC areas 3CD and 5ABCDE and excludes 4B. It is a two-sex Stock Synthesis 3 assessment, ages 1-60, with one combined commercial trawl fishery and five fixed-M composite component runs. Age compositions are plotted in the report; no native run bundle was found in the public source search. Preserve the composite-base-case identity and distinguish its reported exploitation from instantaneous F-at-age.

No canonical 3LNO record exists; this is distinct from the database Georges Bank and Southern New England/Mid-Atlantic yellowtail units. The 2025 assessment is based on data through 2024. Source PDFs and checksums are in source_cache/discovery_dfo_yellowtail_3lno_2025/.

assessment_area: NAFO Division 4T, southern Gulf of St. Lawrence
catch_age_evidence: The official 2025 age-structured assessment uses annual total fishery catch and numbers-at-age proportions by seine and trawl fleet for 1985-2022. survey_age_evidence: The DFO RV survey contributes annual numbers-at-age proportions and an age-aggregated biomass index for 1985-2025. weights_evidence: The assessment uses RV survey weight-at-age for 1985-2025. The official summary identifies a refinement to historical age-length keys; the exact age grid and numeric series remain to be extracted from the detailed report.
maturity_evidence: The assessment uses RV survey maturity-at-age for 1985-2025. The exact age grid, sex treatment and numeric series remain to be extracted.
mortality_evidence: The official state-space model estimates strongly time-varying, age-dependent natural mortality. Reported M groups include ages 4-7, 8-9 and 10+; the detailed report is needed to verify lower-age treatment and process settings.
timing_evidence: The fishery and RV inputs are annual. The DFO RV survey is conducted in September. The model-year definition and within-year observation timing were not verified from the available report text.
output_evidence: The official 2025 assessment reports age-5+ biomass of 8,269 t in 2025, age-1 recruitment, mean F for ages 4-10+, and annual age-group M summaries. decision_reason: DFO identifies NAFO 4T as a single current biological management unit. It is distinct from the existing U.S. Georges Bank and Southern New England/ Mid-Atlantic yellowtail records; no canonical DFO 4T unit exists. The 2025 official assessment provides age compositions, biological age inputs and comparable official population/mortality outputs. Native observations and the reconstruction details remain to be extracted before any canonical import.
notes: Screened from the official 2025 production assessment (Science Response 2026/022) and its detailed Research Document 2026/054.
